The department said it was taking steps to ensure the timely identification of suspected cases, monitoring of individuals who may have been exposed to the virus and provision of appropriate clinical care to affected patients. It urged the public to follow recommended preventive measures and avoid unnecessary panic, stressing that mpox was a preventable and manageable public health concern. The health authorities have directed public and private health care facilities to strictly implement infection prevention and control (IPC) measures to reduce the risk of transmission. Hospitals and other health care establishments have also been advised to ensure the use of personal protective equipment (PPE), wherever indicated, and follow relevant safety protocols while examining and treating suspected or confirmed patients. According to the department, active surveillance and contact tracing are being conducted to identify and monitor individuals who may have come into contact with confirmed cases. Appropriate clinical care is being provided to patients admitted to public hospitals, while healthcare facilities are expected to maintain the required precautions to protect patients, healthcare workers and visitors. The department emphasised that timely detection, effective monitoring and adherence to infection control guidelines were essential to containing the spread of the virus and ensuring that patients received appropriate medical attention. In a separate development, the Sindh Healthcare Commission (SHCC) has sealed Ibn-e-Hassan Hospital in Karachi after a laboratory report confirmed an mpox case in a 20-day-old infant. The action followed concerns regarding infection prevention and control practices at the facility. The development has highlighted the importance of ensuring that healthcare institutions strictly comply with prescribed infection control standards, particularly when dealing with suspected or confirmed infectious diseases. Healthcare facilities have been advised to maintain appropriate safety measures and follow the relevant protocols to minimise the risk of transmission within clinical settings. The health department has also urged citizens to remain vigilant and seek prompt medical assessment if they develop symptoms associated with mpox, including an unusual rash, blisters or skin lesions, particularly after close contact with a suspected or confirmed case. People suspected of having mpox have been advised to avoid close physical contact with others until they have been assessed by a healthcare professional. The health department has also stressed the importance of maintaining good hand hygiene and exercising caution in crowded places, particularly in healthcare facilities. Citizens have been advised to avoid direct contact with skin lesions, rashes or the personal belongings of suspected or confirmed patients. Sharing towels, clothing, bedding and other personal items should also be avoided as a precaution against possible transmission. records.content: EPAPER LIVE TV DAWNNEWS URDU Images Herald Aurora CityFM89 Advertise Events Supplements Careers Obituaries Dawn E-Paper | October 26, 2026 Home Latest US-Iran War Pakistan Opinion Business Images Prism World Sport Breathe Magazines Tech Videos Popular Archive Flood Donations Home Latest US-Iran War Pakistan Opinion Business Images Prism World Sport Breathe Magazines Tech Videos Popular Archive Flood Donations Search Search Subscribe to notifications Get the latest news and updates from Dawn Not Now Allow Notifications First infant battling mpox dies in Karachi hospital Faiza Ilyas Published October 25, 2026 Updated October 25, 2026 10:24am Email Story Your Name * Recipient Email * Send Email Cancel 0 A test tube labelled "Mpox virus positive" is held in this illustration taken August 20, 2024. — Reuters/File comments Join our Whatsapp Channel KARACHI: An infant boy battling mpox for more than a week at a hospital died early on Saturday morning — the first mortality of a baby from the contagious viral infection in Karachi. Sources told Dawn that the 52-day-old baby boy had reportedly contracted the infection during circumcision performed at an “illegal” hospital located in Malir. He remained under treatment at the Sindh Infectious Diseases Hospital & Research Centre (SIDH&RC) for at least 10 days. Speaking on the condition of anonymity, a senior doctor at the hospital said that another infant patient with mpox was still in critical condition. “His key health indicators are not good. The information gathered from his parents indicates that he too underwent circumcision at the Malir hospital that has been officially sealed recently over concerns related to lack of infection control measures,” he said. Death takes Sindh’s tally to 12, with 98 cases reported so far this year According to the sources, at least seven patients, including a SIDH&RC worker who is believed to have contracted the infection from the hospital, are currently under treatment for mpox at the healthcare facility. They all are residents of Karachi. These cases include two workers employed at the fruit and vegetable market on Superhighway and a female patient, who reportedly contracted the infection from her husband. First infant’s death in city The sources said the latest death is the first death of an infant in Karachi. Earlier, two patients with chronic lung and kidney diseases were admitted to the SIDH&RC with mpox. They died during treatment but their chronic illnesses were recorded as the cause of their deaths. With the latest death, the total number of mpox deaths recorded this year in Sindh has risen to 12 with 98 cases reported so far. The sources said nearly all victims were either infants or newborns who contracted the infection from hospital/clinic settings lacking infection control protocols. In April, an outbreak of mpox, which was earlier restricted to patients with a history of foreign travel, was reported from Khairpur, claiming the lives of at least seven infants. The babies were under treatment in the intensive care units of two hospitals. Investigations showed that these facilities lacked infection control protocols. The district of Sukkur also saw two infants’ deaths from mpox. Sources of transmission According to experts, mpox transmission occurs through close contact with someone who has mpox, contaminated bedding, towels, medical instruments, surfaces or objects. “People with mpox can spread it to animals or vice versa through close contact. Vertical and perinatal transmission is possible as well. Some people are infectious 1-4 days before getting symptomatic,” said Dr Samreen Sarfaraz, consultant infectious diseases and the Chairperson of Infection Control Services at the Indus Hospital. Most patients, she said, recover fully within 2-4 weeks without treatment, while some develop complications. “A patient remains infectious till his or her rashes are completely healed (and a fresh layer of healthy intact skin has formed underneath),” she said. Prof Faisal Mahmood, senior infectious disease specialist at the Aga Khan University Hospital, said that mpox can spread through the air to a limited extent, but only when lesions or material from lesions are aerosolised. “This may happen when a sample is taken or when lesions are in or around the airway. Compared with chickenpox, mpox is much less contagious. Chickenpox can spread through the air over a considerable distance and does not require direct contact. The same applies to measles,” he said. He further added: “Mpox outbreaks can occur where infection prevention and control measures, such as environmental cleaning, are suboptimal, or where people are in close quarters or have significant body-to-body contact.” It might be recalled that the Sindh Health Care Commission has recently sealed Ibn-i-Hassan Hospital at Malir 15 following a laboratory report confirming an mpox case in an infant, after concerns were identified regarding infection prevention and control practices. records.content: News Health Two more mpox cases reported in Pakistan’s Sindh province — The Express Tribune UA.NEWS 24 October 2026 06:28 Two new cases of mpox, also known as monkeypox, have been reported in Pakistan’s Sindh province. The total number of confirmed infections in the province has risen to 98. Seven new cases have been detected there over the past week. Contact tracing Sindh’s Health Department has stepped up surveillance, contact tracing and patient support, The Express Tribune reports . Authorities are locating and monitoring people who came into contact with infected individuals to contain the spread of the virus. Public and private healthcare facilities have been instructed to strictly follow infection prevention and control measures. Residents were also advised to wash their hands thoroughly and avoid direct contact with rashes, blisters and sores on people with suspected or confirmed mpox. More current news is available on the UA.News Telegram channel Telegram . Recommendations for the public Medical professionals urged people not to share towels, clothing or bedding with infected individuals. People who develop unusual rashes or blisters were advised to seek medical care immediately and inform doctors about possible contact with a patient suspected of having mpox. Earlier this month, The Express Tribune reported 95 confirmed mpox cases and 11 deaths in Sindh. The disease has also been recorded among Karachi residents with no history of foreign travel. Mpox can be transmitted through close physical contact, skin lesions and contaminated personal items. Possible symptoms include fever, body aches, swollen lymph nodes, rashes or blisters. Subscribe More forecasts: Atlanta 30 day forecast Las Vegas/ Crime & Emergencies Clark County Confirms First Clade I Mpox Case Without Reported Travel Exposure By James Thompson Published on October 20, 2026 Source: Google Street View A Clark County resident has tested positive for clade I mpox, the more severe strain of the virus, and health officials say the person had no reported travel exposure. The Southern Nevada Health District confirmed the case this week, marking the first time the clade I strain has turned up in a local resident without a clear travel link. The health district reported the case as part of a broader update on mpox activity in the Las Vegas area, according to KSNV. Since the virus was first detected locally in June 2022, Clark County has logged 365 total mpox cases, according to the Southern Nevada Health District. The district also noted that 11 confirmed clade II cases have surfaced locally between August and October 2026, a sign of increased virus activity heading into the clade I discovery. No Clear Source of Exposure SNHD has said the individual diagnosed with clade I mpox has no reported travel exposure, leaving the source of transmission unclear. Dr. Cassius Lockett, the district's health officer, said mpox continues to circulate in the community and encouraged people at risk to get vaccinated and those potentially exposed to seek guidance promptly. Lockett also said that recognizing symptoms early and avoiding close contact with others while sick can help prevent further spread, per the same report from the health district. Clade I and clade II are the two viral types behind mpox illness. Clade II caused the global outbreak that began in 2022 and continues to circulate at low levels across the U.S., while clade I spread widely across Central and Eastern Africa in 2024 before cases began appearing in other countries, including the United States, the health district's report notes. Why Clade I Draws Closer Scrutiny The heightened concern around clade I stems from its track record overseas. According to the Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health, clade I mpox has historically produced case fatality rates between 1% and 10% in African outbreaks, compared with less than 1% to 4% for clade II. The World Health Organization declared clade I a Public Health Emergency of International Concern in August 2024 amid a rapid surge of the clade Ib strain across Central and Eastern Africa, its second such mpox declaration. Clade I's arrival in the U.S. has followed a steady progression. The first known American case was confirmed in a traveler returning from Eastern Africa to California in November 2024, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Nearly a year later, in October 2025, Long Beach, California recorded the nation's first locally acquired clade I case in a patient with no travel history, as reported by CIDRAP. Similar travel-linked and non-travel cases have since surfaced elsewhere, including in Arizona and San Diego County. Vaccine and Exposure Guidance Health officials emphasize that the Jynneos vaccine is expected to protect against both clade I and clade II mpox, and SNHD continues to offer it at its immunization clinics. By August 2024, clinics affiliated with the health district had already administered more than 11,740 doses across Clark County, reflecting the scale of earlier vaccination efforts following the 2022 outbreak. The standard Jynneos regimen for adults 18 and older requires two doses spaced four weeks, or 28 days, apart to achieve full protection, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. For those who may have been exposed, the agency says post-exposure vaccination works best within four days of exposure, though getting the shot between four and 14 days afterward can still reduce how severe symptoms become. Anyone potentially exposed should monitor for symptoms for 21 days following their last contact, per SNHD guidance. How Mpox Spreads and What Symptoms Look Like Mpox spreads primarily through close, sustained physical contact, including direct contact with rash, sores, scabs or bodily fluids, as well as through kissing or oral, anal or vaginal sex. It can also spread through contaminated clothing, bedding or towels, and through pregnancy or childbirth. Symptoms usually begin within three weeks of exposure and the illness typically lasts two to four weeks, with a rash that may appear on or near the genitals or anus, or on the hands, feet, chest, face or mouth. Other symptoms can include fever, chills, swollen lymph nodes, headache, muscle aches and fatigue, though some people develop only a rash without any other symptoms. Anyone with suspected or confirmed mpox is advised to stay home and avoid close contact with others, including household members and pets, and to avoid sexual contact, kissing and other close physical contact. If contact with others is unavoidable, health officials recommend wearing a well-fitting mask and completely covering rashes and sores with clothing or bandages. People with mpox should also avoid sharing clothing, bedding, towels and other personal items, and should wash their hands frequently with soap and water, especially after touching the rash, using an alcohol-based hand sanitizer when soap and water aren't available. Isolation should continue until all sores have healed, scabs have fallen off and a fresh layer of skin has formed, per the health district's guidance. records.content: News Health A 52-day-old boy receiving treatment for mpox dies in Karachi — Dawn UA.NEWS 25 October 2026 08:09 A 52-day-old boy died in Karachi, Pakistan, after receiving treatment for mpox for more than a week at the Sindh Infectious Diseases Hospital & Research Centre. This is the first infant death from this viral infection in the city, Dawn reports . According to the publication's sources, the child may have been infected during a circumcision performed at a hospital in the Malir district. The medical facility was later sealed by the Sindh Healthcare Commission over concerns about failure to comply with infection-control measures. Another infant in critical condition A doctor at the medical facility, who spoke to journalists anonymously, said that another infant with mpox is in critical condition. According to information obtained from the parents, this child also underwent circumcision at a hospital in Malir. As Dawn writes, at least seven patients with mpox are being treated at the Sindh Infectious Diseases Hospital & Research Centre, including a hospital employee who was likely infected at work. All of them are residents of Karachi. The patients also include two workers from the fruit and vegetable market on Super Highway and a woman who reportedly contracted the infection from her husband. More current news is available on the UA.News Telegram channel Telegram . 98 cases in Sindh this year Following the boy's death, the number of mpox deaths recorded this year in Sindh province rose to 12, while the number of detected cases reached 98. The publication's sources say that nearly all those who died were infants or newborns who became infected in hospitals or clinics without proper infection-control protocols. In April, an mpox outbreak was recorded in the Khairpur district, where at least seven infants died. An investigation found that the two hospitals where they were in intensive care units lacked adequate infection-control measures. Two more infant deaths from mpox were recorded in Sukkur district. Experts note that mpox is transmitted through close contact with an infected person, as well as through contaminated bedding, towels, medical instruments, surfaces and objects. Most patients recover within two to four weeks, but the infection can cause complications. Read us on Download our app

has confirmed four new mpox cases in South Africa, bringing the total number of laboratory-confirmed cases reported since 1 January 2026 to 26. Check Symptoms The cases are spread across five provinces, with the Western Cape recording the highest number at 18. Gauteng has reported three cases, while the Eastern Cape and Free State have recorded two each. KwaZulu-Natal has reported one case. Of the 18 cases in the Western Cape, two involved foreign nationals visiting South Africa who contracted the virus abroad, while the remaining 16 were linked to local transmission. According to the department, 25 of the 26 confirmed cases involve men aged between 23 and 50, with a median age of 37. The department said it would continue working with the National Institute for Communicable Diseases, provincial health authorities and other stakeholders to strengthen surveillance, identify cases, trace contacts and improve public awareness to prevent further transmission. Buy Maps Clade and lineage information is available for 17 cases. Of these, 13 are associated with the Clade Ib mpox virus and four with Clade IIb. The department has urged members of the public to remain vigilant and seek medical attention promptly if they develop symptoms, including a rash, fever, headache, muscle aches, swollen lymph nodes or fatigue. People who have been in close contact with a confirmed or suspected mpox case are advised to inform healthcare workers and monitor themselves for symptoms for 21 days. “Should symptoms develop, they should avoid close contact with others and seek medical attention,” the department said in a statement. Mpox is a preventable and treatable viral infection. The public is advised to avoid close, skin-to-skin contact with anyone who has an mpox-like rash and not to share bedding, towels, clothing or other personal items with affected individuals. Healthcare workers have also been urged to remain alert to possible cases and follow infection prevention and control protocols when treating suspected infections. records.content: Infant dies of mpox in Pakistan's Sindh-Xinhua Infant dies of mpox in Pakistan's Sindh Source: Xinhua Editor: huaxia 2026-10-25 16:22:15 ISLAMABAD, Oct. 25 (Xinhua) -- A 53-day-old infant died of mpox in Pakistan's southern Sindh province on Saturday, raising the death toll from the disease in the province to 12 this year, health officials said. The infant, a resident of Karachi's Malir district, was transferred to the Sindh Infectious Diseases Hospital and Research Center (SIDH&RC) after developing symptoms following a circumcision procedure at a private hospital, the facility's medical superintendent, Abdul Wahid Rajput, told local media. Rajput confirmed that mpox was the cause of death. The Sindh Healthcare Commission (SHCC) has sealed Ibn-e-Hassan Hospital in Malir, where the procedure was performed, after an investigation found inadequate infection prevention and control measures, poor hygiene and unqualified staff, according to an official statement. The commission said the infant contracted the virus through contaminated scissors used during the procedure. Laboratory testing confirmed the infection. Separately, the Sindh health department reported two more mpox cases on Friday, bringing the provincial tally to 98. Authorities have stepped up surveillance, contact tracing and infection-control measures to curb the spread of the virus. Mpox can spread through close physical contact with infected people and contaminated items. Symptoms include fever, body aches, swollen lymph nodes and skin rashes or blisters. ■ Infant dies of mpox in Pakistan's Sindh

Society Five patients ‘test positive for mpox’ in Russia’s St. Petersburg The patients were placed under observation last week after they were suspected of contracting the disease Maria Kamińska Edited by: Ed Wight 20.10.2026, 10:19 All five patiens are in stable condition. Photo Illustration: PAP/Albert Zawada Five patients hospitalized with suspected mpox in St. Petersburg have tested positive for the virus, according to local health authorities. The patients were placed under observation last week after they were suspected of contracting the disease. All five are in stable condition and have mild to moderate symptoms, Russia’s state news agency TASS reported on Monday, citing Botkin Infectious Diseases Hospital in St. Petersburg, where they are receiving treatment. Mpox, formerly known as monkeypox, is a viral disease that can cause flu-like symptoms, including fever, headache and muscle aches, as well as skin lesions. It is endemic in parts of Africa and spreads primarily through direct contact with infected person or animal. Although the disease can be fatal, most infections are mild and resolve within two to four weeks. Russia’s consumer health watchdog, Rospotrebnadzor, said authorities were tracing the patients’ contacts and implementing measures to prevent further spread. It remains unclear where or how the patients contracted the virus. In a separate incident, five people in the Moscow region were placed under medical observation after coming into contact with someone suspected of having mpox, Russian news agency Interfax reported on October 15, citing local health authorities. In 2024, the World Health Organization declared mpox a public health emergency of international concern after a rise in cases. First a plague, now monkeypox: Putin faces new outbreak across two cities Kathrine Frich • October 20, 2026 Follow dagens.com on Google Shutterstock.com These new cases arrive right on the heels of another health scare in Russia. Others are reading now Georgetown professor warns Europe to confront Trump as a pro-Russian president Russia targets Kyiv water supply according to Kremlin documents Keeping rare illnesses out of major cities is a constant race against the clock for health workers. Modern travel makes it easy for viruses to cross borders before anyone spots the first symptom. Now, hospital wards in two major metropolitan areas are dealing with a fresh cluster of cases. Hospital beds fill up Four people in St. Petersburg have tested positive for monkeypox, according to Latvian news outlet LA.LV and Ukrainian portal Dialog.ua. Also read Instagram is officially burying fake AI influencers who refuse to label their posts 401(k) creator says many workers need another way to save All four residents are now in a local hospital. Russian media outlets report that doctors consider their condition moderately serious. The alert goes beyond Russia’s second-largest city. In the Moscow region, medics admitted five more people to a hospital after they came into contact with a suspected monkeypox patient, LA.LV reported. Sergei Markitan, the head doctor at Ramensky Hospital, stated that these five patients are in satisfactory condition while they stay under medical watch. At the time of his update, Markitan noted that doctors were still waiting for lab test results ordered by Rospotrebnadzor, Russia’s consumer health watchdog. According to information from the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) cited by LA.LV, monkeypox is a rare virus most often seen in Central and West Africa. It spreads from rodents and primates to humans, and symptoms usually show up between five and 21 days after infection. Earlier cases and denials This is not the first time the virus has hit Russia this year. Back in February, health officials tracked cases in both the Moscow region and St. Petersburg, Dialog.ua reported. Doctors at Domodedovo Hospital confirmed one man had the virus and admitted a close contact the very next day, followed two weeks later by two tourists returning to St. Petersburg from Thailand. These new cases arrive right on the heels of another health scare in Russia. In early October, an employee at the Irkutsk Plague Research Institute in Siberia died, sparking widespread rumours of a plague outbreak, according to LA.LV. Moscow quickly pushed back against those claims. Russian officials insisted the woman died of severe pneumonia and maintained that lab tests showed no dangerous germs. Still, the World Health Organization stated on October 10 that the exact cause of her death remains unknown, though the agency sees no signs that the illness is spreading. The sample was tested at Dow Laboratory, where it reportedly returned positive for mpox. Following the report, SHCC officials, with the support of the DHO Korangi and the SSP Korangi, took immediate action and sealed the hospital. The quack resisted the SHCC officials and called his supporters to prevent them from carrying out their official duties. The action was taken over poor hygiene, inadequate infection prevention and control (IPC) measures, and reported malpractices that raised serious concerns about patient safety and public health.
